2027-02-24.title: Third Wednesday of the Great Fast
2027-02-24.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Do not repay evil for evil, but repay with a blessing
2027-02-24.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-24.verse: But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
theo: Peter writes to small Christian communities scattered across Asia Minor, minorities who were mocked, slandered and sometimes threatened by their neighbours. He does not teach them how to hit back. He describes a community: “Finally, all of you, have unity of spirit, sympathy, love for one another, a tender heart, and a humble mind.” Then the hard part: “Do not repay evil for evil or abuse for abuse; but, on the contrary, repay with a blessing.” The world runs on the law of return: you insult me, I insult you; you ignore me, I ignore you. Peter asks Christians to break the circle by returning something better than what they received. He reminds them that blessing is their own calling, “that you might inherit a blessing”, and he quotes the psalm: “let them keep their tongues from evil and their lips from speaking deceit; let them turn away from evil and do good; let them seek peace and pursue it.” Peace is not something we wait for; it has to be pursued, like someone running after a friend who has walked away. The Great Fast is a fast of the tongue as well as of the stomach. A day without meat is easy compared with a day without a sharp reply.

In the Gospel Jesus goes further still: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous.” Kerala knows this picture well: when the rain comes it falls on every compound, on the house of the saint and the house of the sinner, on the field of the friend and the field of the enemy. That is how God loves. “For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?” Love that only returns love is ordinary; Christian love begins where the return stops. Then the summit of the Sermon: “Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.” Perfect here means whole, a love with no one left out. We may not feel love for an enemy, but we can pray for him, and prayer is where love begins. Jesus himself prayed from the Cross for those who crucified him: “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing” (Luke 23:34). Tomorrow the Syro-Malabar Church honours a daughter of Kerala whose family lived these words to the end.

Sun and rain on the evil and the good.

live: Write down the name of one person who has hurt you, and pray for that person every evening until Easter.
Fast from the sharp reply (1 Peter 3:9)
Today, when you are insulted or ignored, answer with a blessing or with silence.
2027-02-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, from the Cross you prayed for those who crucified you. Give us a tender heart and a humble mind, teach us not to repay evil for evil but to answer with a blessing, and make us children of the Father who sends his sun and rain on all. Make our love whole, with no one left out, and give us peace to pursue and to share. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we receive the Body of the Lord who gave himself for his enemies; we cannot receive him and refuse to pray for ours.

quick: Peter: do not repay evil for evil, but repay with a blessing.
Jesus: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.
God's sun and rain fall on everyone; our love must leave no one out.
2027-02-24.action: Pray by name today for one person who has hurt you.
2027-02-24.question: Whom have I left out of my love and my prayer?

family.explain: Jesus says: it is easy to love people who love us. But God wants us to love even people who are unkind to us, and to pray for them. God sends the sunshine and the rain on everyone, good and bad. We are his children when we love like that.
family.intention: We pray for someone who has been unkind to one of us.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school, at work or in the neighbourhood we find hard to like? Let us pray for them together now.”

illus: A nurse from Thodupuzha working in a Gulf hospital had a supervisor who seemed to find fault with everything she did. During the Great Fast she wrote the supervisor's name on a slip of paper, kept it in her prayer book, and prayed for her every night. Nothing changed for weeks. Then, in Holy Week, the supervisor stopped her in the corridor, her eyes red, and said: my mother is very ill at home; I know you pray; will you pray for her? The nurse said: I have been praying for you for forty days already.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you prayed for your enemies. Soften our hearts as we pray now. Amen.
share: Repay with a blessing (1 Peter 3:9). Where am I caught in the circle of returning evil?
Seek peace and pursue it (1 Peter 3:11). What peace do I need to run after?
Love your enemies (Matthew 5:44). Whose name do I find hardest to say in prayer?
interc: For the Church, that she may answer hatred with blessing.
For those who persecute Christians, that they may come to know Christ.
For families divided by quarrels over property and inheritance.
For those who have hurt us, and those we have hurt.
For our group, that we may be children of our Father in heaven.
pm.close: Father, you make your sun rise on the evil and on the good. Make us perfect as you are perfect, loving without exception. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Peter asks us for a tender heart and a humble mind. And he adds: do not repay evil for evil or abuse for abuse; but, on the contrary, repay with a blessing (1 Peter 3:9).

The world runs on the law of return. You hurt me, I hurt you. Peter asks us to break the circle. The Great Fast is also a fast of the tongue: a day without meat is easy compared with a day without a sharp reply.

Jesus goes further: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). God sends his sun and rain on the good and the bad alike. If we love only those who love us, what is special about that?

We may not feel love for an enemy, but we can pray for him. Prayer is where love begins. Jesus prayed on the Cross: Father, forgive them (Luke 23:34). Let us choose one name today, and pray for that person every day until Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asks us to pray even for people who are unkind to us. Tonight, can you say a little prayer for someone who was not nice to you? That is how God's children love!

intro: Theme: “But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
The blessing that breaks the circle of evil, peace that must be pursued, and the whole love of the Father.

sub: A tender heart and a humble mind.
q: Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.

points.apply: Answer the next insult with a blessing, or with silence and a prayer.

sub: What more are you doing than others?
A love with no one left out.
q: Speak to all the congregation of the people of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
points.apply: Do one quiet kindness this week for someone who does not like you.

concl: Christian love begins where the return stops.
Bless, pray, and let your love fall like the rain, on everyone.
